cweDef.name: Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input
cweDef.summary: Unbounded copy and allocation calls overflow their destination when input exceeds its size.

title: Unbounded buffer call {sink} ({lang}) — review required
description: The {lang} call {sink} copies or allocates without a destination bound. Oversized input overflows into adjacent memory. This lexical rule flags the call; the reviewer confirms bounded use or replaces it with {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on the {sink} call in {lang} code.
fp: Fixed small inputs are the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} copies or formats into a destination without a size bound, so input longer than that destination overwrites adjacent memory. The remedy is a bounded variant ({safe}) plus an explicit length check.
fix: Re-run the scan and confirm none remains on untrusted input.
verifyT: Rescan shows no unbounded call on untrusted input.

title: Unbounded scanf conversion ({lang}) — review required
description: A {lang} scan uses an unbounded string conversion: {sink}. Input longer than the buffer overflows it. This lexical rule flags the conversion; the reviewer bounds it via {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on scanf conversions in {lang} code.
fp: Fixed-format input is the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} reads a string without a width limit, so a long token overruns the destination buffer. The remedy is a conversion that carries a width ({safe}) and a check on the input length.
risk: Stack or heap overflow; HIGH severity.
verifyT: Rescan shows no unbounded conversion.

cweDef.name: Execution with Unnecessary Privileges
cweDef.summary: Privilege-changing calls grant powers the process may not need for its whole lifetime.

title: Privilege or root change via {sink} ({lang}) — review required
description: The {lang} call {sink} changes privilege or filesystem root. Mistakes lock in excessive power or an escapable jail. This lexical rule flags the call; the reviewer confirms the drop order and confinement via {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on the {sink} call in {lang} code.
fp: Correct privilege drops are the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} alters privilege or root. The check is {safe}.
risk: Excess privilege or jail escape; MEDIUM severity.
verifyT: Review confirms least privilege.

c:chroot: chdir plus closed descriptors after chroot

title: Umask cleared to zero ({lang}) — review required
description: The process clears its umask: {sink}. New files then keep group and world permissions. This lexical rule flags the clearing; the reviewer restores {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on umask clearing in {lang} code.
fp: Brief scoped clearing is the rare accepted case.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} removes the permission mask. The remedy is {safe}.
applicability: {lang} code setting umask; single-line lexical scope.
risk: World-readable or writable files; MEDIUM severity.
verifyT: Rescan shows no cleared umask.

cweDef.name: Time-of-check Time-of-use Race Condition
cweDef.summary: Checking a file before using it leaves a window where the file can be swapped.

title: Pre-check file access via {sink} ({lang}) — review required
description: The {lang} call {sink} checks a file before use. An attacker swaps the file between check and use. This lexical rule flags the check; the reviewer opens atomically via {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on the {sink} call in {lang} code.
fp: Display-only checks are the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} pre-checks files. The remedy is {safe}.
verifyT: Rescan shows no pre-check before use.

title: Expression evaluation via {sink} ({lang}) — review required
description: The {lang} call {sink} evaluates expressions. Untrusted input becomes code execution. This lexical rule flags the call; the reviewer confirms trust or removes it via {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on the {sink} call in {lang} code.
fp: Fixed expressions are the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} evaluates an expression supplied at runtime, which turns untrusted text into executable code inside the application process. The remedy is to remove evaluation and call the intended operation directly ({safe}).
verifyT: Rescan shows no sink on untrusted input.

title: Script evaluation ({fw}) — review required
description: A {fw} engine evaluates a string: {sink}. Untrusted input becomes code execution. This lexical rule flags the evaluation; the reviewer confirms trust or removes it via {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on script evaluation ({fw}).
fp: Fixed scripts are the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {fw}, {sink} evaluates a string as a script, so any value the attacker can place in that string runs with the application's privileges. The remedy is to eliminate string evaluation and dispatch on a fixed set of operations ({safe}).
verifyT: Rescan shows no evaluation on untrusted input.

title: Unsafe decoding via {sink} ({lang}) — review required
description: The {lang} call {sink} rebuilds objects from bytes. Hostile input instantiates gadget chains. This lexical rule flags the call; the reviewer confirms trust or hardens via {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on the {sink} call in {lang} code.
fp: Trusted local data is the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} rebuilds objects from a byte stream, so a crafted stream can instantiate classes the author never intended to expose. The remedy is to accept only a constrained format with an allowlist ({safe}).
verifyT: Rescan shows no raw call on untrusted bytes.

java:schema: secure processing plus no external access

title: SnakeYAML unsafe load ({lang}) — review required
description: SnakeYAML loads untrusted documents: {sink}. Unsafe constructors instantiate arbitrary classes. This lexical rule flags the load; the reviewer confirms trust or uses {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on YAML loads in {lang} code.
fp: Trusted config is the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} loads YAML unsafely. The remedy is {safe}.
verifyT: Rescan shows no unsafe load on untrusted input.

title: TLS trust weakened ({fw}) — review required
description: TLS trust is weakened: {sink} ({fw}). Disabled checks and fixed secrets let attackers impersonate servers or authenticate. This lexical rule flags the weakness; the reviewer restores {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on TLS trust code ({fw}).
fp: Test fixtures are the common false positive.
recordDesc: With {sink}, {fw} TLS trust is weakened. The remedy is {safe}.
verifyT: Rescan shows no weakened trust outside tests.

java:emptytrust: public void checkServerTrusted(X509Certificate[] c, String a) {}
public void checkServerTrusted(X509Certificate[] c, String a) { throw new RuntimeException(); }

title: Cleartext protocol client ({fw}) — review required
description: Code uses a cleartext client: {sink} ({fw}). Credentials and data travel unencrypted. This lexical rule flags the client; the reviewer migrates to {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on cleartext clients ({fw}).
fp: Loopback use is the common accepted case.
recordDesc: With {sink}, {fw} opens a cleartext connection, so credentials and payloads cross the network readable to anyone on the path. The remedy is a TLS-wrapped client ({safe}) with certificate verification enabled.
risk: Credential and data theft; MEDIUM severity.
verifyT: Rescan shows no cleartext client.

title: Dynamic execution via {sink} ({lang}) — review required
description: The {lang} call {sink} runs commands, code, or native libraries. Untrusted input becomes execution. This lexical rule flags the call; the reviewer confirms trust or replaces it with {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on the {sink} call in {lang} code.
fp: Trusted tooling is the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} executes a command, expression or native library chosen at runtime, so a value reaching it becomes code in the process. The remedy is a fixed call path with argument passing ({safe}).
risk: Command or code execution; HIGH severity.
verifyT: Rescan shows no sink on untrusted input.

title: Dangerous function {sink} ({lang}) — review required
description: The {lang} call {sink} evaluates code, invokes by name, or uses a removed database extension. Untrusted input becomes execution or failure. This lexical rule flags the call; the reviewer removes it via {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on the {sink} call in {lang} code.
fp: Legacy shims are the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} evaluates code, dispatches by name or depends on a removed extension, so a runtime value decides what executes. The remedy is to delete the dynamic evaluation and call the concrete function ({safe}).
risk: Code execution or breakage; HIGH severity.
verifyT: Rescan shows no call remains.

title: Dangerous PHP construct ({fw}) — review required
description: PHP evaluates or includes dynamically: {sink} ({fw}). Backticks run shells, variable includes load attacker paths, extract and parse_str overwrite variables, and /e evaluates replacements. This lexical rule flags the construct; the reviewer removes it via {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on dangerous constructs ({fw}).
fp: Trusted local use is the common false positive.
recordDesc: With {sink}, {fw} evaluates or includes dynamically. The remedy is {safe}.
risk: Code execution or inclusion; HIGH severity.
verifyT: Rescan shows no construct on untrusted input.

title: Weak PHP crypto or diagnostics ({fw}) — review required
description: PHP weakens crypto or diagnostics: {sink} ({fw}). ECB leaks patterns, low bcrypt cost speeds guessing, silenced errors hide attacks, and register_globals resurrects variable injection. This lexical rule flags the setting; the reviewer hardens via {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on PHP settings ({fw}).
fp: Legacy interop is the common false positive.
recordDesc: With {sink}, {fw} crypto or diagnostics are weak. The remedy is {safe}.
verifyT: Rescan shows no weak setting.

php:ecb.recordDesc: AES in ECB mode encrypts identical plaintext blocks into identical ciphertext blocks and adds no integrity check.
php:ecb.risk: A reader of the ciphertext sees repetition and block structure, and can splice blocks without detection; MEDIUM because the attacker first needs the stored data.

php:cost.recordDesc: bcrypt with a cost parameter of 4 runs the key-derivation function 256 times, which a GPU exhausts quickly.
php:cost.risk: A stolen hash dump is cracked at billions of guesses per second, so the dump becomes plaintext passwords; MEDIUM because it needs prior disclosure of the hashes.

php:erroff.recordDesc: error_reporting(0) suppresses notices, warnings and fatals before they reach the error log.
php:erroff.risk: Failures and hostile requests leave no record, so incident review loses the only trace of what the application did; MEDIUM because the setting itself exposes nothing.

php:regglobals.recordDesc: register_globals = On turns request parameters into PHP variables in every script scope.
php:regglobals.risk: A request can overwrite variables the script never meant to expose, which turns a query string into control flow; MEDIUM.

php:pdo.recordDesc: $pdo->query interpolates the statement string instead of binding parameters, so the value becomes SQL syntax.
php:pdo.risk: A request value that reaches the interpolated fragment reads other rows or drops tables; MEDIUM because exploitation depends on where the string is built.

title: Dynamic evaluation via {sink} ({lang}) — review required
description: The {lang} call {sink} resolves, renders, or loads dynamically. Untrusted input becomes code execution or unsafe output. This lexical rule flags the call; the reviewer confirms trust or replaces it with {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on the {sink} call in {lang} code.
fp: Trusted templates are the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} resolves, renders or loads at runtime, so a value that reaches it selects the code path or markup that is produced. The remedy is an explicit branch over known operations with escaping ({safe}).
risk: Code execution or XSS; HIGH severity.
verifyT: Rescan shows no sink on untrusted input.

title: ActiveRecord SQL from input ({fw}) — review required
description: Rails builds SQL from input: {sink} ({fw}). Interpolated fragments rewrite the statement. This lexical rule flags the assembly; the reviewer parameterizes via {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: any assembled query matches.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on assembled SQL ({fw}).
fp: Fixed fragments are the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {fw}, {sink} mixes SQL with values. The remedy is {safe}.
verifyT: Rescan shows no assembled query on untrusted input.

title: Sandbox escape via {sink} ({lang}) — review required
description: The {lang} call {sink} runs code inside a context. Contexts are not security boundaries, so untrusted input becomes execution. This lexical rule flags the call; the reviewer confirms trust or removes it via {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on the {sink} call in {lang} code.
fp: Trusted plugins are the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} runs strings as code. The remedy is {safe}.
verifyT: Rescan shows no sink on untrusted input.

title: Dangerous JS construct ({fw}) — review required
description: JavaScript evaluates or trusts dynamically: {sink} ({fw}). String timers and Function compile code, shell spawn runs commands, variable require loads paths, __proto__ assignment pollutes prototypes, and bypassSecurityTrustHtml drops sanitization. This lexical rule flags the construct; the reviewer removes it via {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on dangerous constructs ({fw}).
fp: Trusted local use is the common false positive.
recordDesc: With {sink}, {fw} evaluates or trusts dynamically. The remedy is {safe}.
risk: Code execution or pollution; HIGH severity.
verifyT: Rescan shows no construct on untrusted input.

cweDef.name: Improper Verification of Source of Communication Channel
cweDef.summary: Broadcasting messages or fetching over cleartext lets any party read or alter the exchange.

title: Overly broad browser channel ({fw}) — review required
description: Browser code broadcasts or fetches broadly: {sink} ({fw}). postMessage to any origin leaks data to hostile frames, and ws:// sockets expose traffic. This lexical rule flags the channel; the reviewer narrows it via {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on browser channels ({fw}).
fp: Public broadcasts are the common accepted case.
recordDesc: With {sink}, {fw} exposes a broad channel. The remedy is {safe}.
risk: Data leak or interception; MEDIUM severity.
verifyT: Rescan shows no broad channel.

title: Dynamic load via {sink} ({lang}) — review required
description: The {lang} call {sink} loads plugins, replaces the process image, or marks strings as safe HTML. Untrusted input becomes code or script. This lexical rule flags the call; the reviewer confirms trust or replaces it with {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on the {sink} call in {lang} code.
fp: Trusted plugins are the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} loads a plugin, replaces the process image or marks a string as trusted HTML, so the value decides what code runs or what the browser renders. The remedy is a fixed, reviewed call ({safe}).
risk: Code execution or XSS; HIGH severity.
verifyT: Rescan shows no sink on untrusted input.

title: Go Exec built by concatenation ({lang}) — review required
description: A {lang} Exec call assembles SQL: {sink}. Untrusted parts rewrite the statement. This lexical rule flags the assembly; the reviewer parameterizes via {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: any assembled statement matches.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on assembled SQL in {lang} code.
fp: Fixed fragments are the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} assembles SQL by concatenation, so a value in the string can rewrite the statement's structure. The remedy is a parameterized query ({safe}), never string formatting of values.
verifyT: Rescan shows no assembled statement on untrusted input.

title: Unsafe .NET call {sink} ({lang}) — review required
description: The {lang} call {sink} deserializes, parses XML, or writes raw HTML. Hostile input becomes gadgets or script. This lexical rule flags the call; the reviewer confirms trust or replaces it with {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on the {sink} call in {lang} code.
fp: Trusted local data is the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} deserializes bytes, parses XML with a resolver or writes raw HTML, so the input decides which types instantiate or what the browser executes. The remedy is a hardened, typed API ({safe}).
verifyT: Rescan shows no call on untrusted input.

title: Dangerous .NET construct ({fw}) — review required
description: .NET weakens a control: {sink} ({fw}). Polymorphic typing enables gadgets, XSLT scripts execute, certificate callbacks accept all, plaintext mail and HTTP leak data, and validation opt-outs invite script. This lexical rule flags the construct; the reviewer hardens via {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on .NET constructs ({fw}).
fp: Trusted local use is the common false positive.
recordDesc: With {sink}, {fw} relaxes a security control such as polymorphic binding, certificate validation or output encoding, so the weakened path accepts data it should reject. The remedy is to restore the strict setting ({safe}).
verifyT: Rescan shows no weak construct.

csharp:typenames.recordDesc: TypeNameHandling.All makes Json.NET read the .NET type name out of the payload and instantiate that type, so the document decides which class is constructed.
csharp:typenames.risk: A crafted payload picks its own type and can reach gadget chains already loaded in the process, which turns document deserialisation into code execution; HIGH severity.

csharp:xslscript.recordDesc: EnableScript = true lets an XSLT transform run embedded script while it processes the source document.
csharp:xslscript.risk: A transform fed attacker-influenced XML executes that script inside the application process, so the boundary between data and code no longer exists; HIGH severity.

csharp:certcb.recordDesc: ServerCertificateValidationCallback that returns true accepts every server certificate, including self-signed, expired and mismatched ones.
csharp:certcb.risk: Any on-path attacker can present their own certificate and impersonate the endpoint, reading and rewriting the traffic on that connection; HIGH severity.

csharp:webclient.recordDesc: WebClient.DownloadString over a plain http:// URL fetches content with no transport protection.
csharp:webclient.risk: The fetched body is readable and replaceable in transit, so configuration, scripts or payloads pulled this way cannot be trusted; HIGH severity.

csharp:smtp.recordDesc: EnableSsl = false makes SmtpClient open the session in cleartext instead of starting TLS.
csharp:smtp.risk: Credentials and message bodies cross the network unencrypted, so a network observer captures them; HIGH severity.

csharp:sqlinterp.recordDesc: An interpolated string is handed straight to SqlCommand, so the statement text is assembled from runtime values.
csharp:sqlinterp.risk: An interpolated value becomes SQL syntax, which gives an injectable path to reading and modifying the database; HIGH severity.

csharp:sqlconcat.recordDesc: The SqlCommand text is built by string concatenation, so the statement is assembled from runtime values.
csharp:sqlconcat.risk: A quote in a concatenated value changes the statement that executes, which is the classic SQL injection shape; HIGH severity.

csharp:validatereq.recordDesc: ValidateRequest="false" disables ASP.NET request validation for the page, the check that rejects markup in submitted values before the action runs.
csharp:validatereq.risk: Submitted markup reaches the response unless every consumer encodes it, which is how reflected and stored XSS begins; HIGH severity.

csharp:validateinput.recordDesc: [ValidateInput(false)] disables ASP.NET request validation for one action or controller.
csharp:validateinput.risk: The action accepts markup in its inputs, so any view that renders those values without encoding becomes an XSS sink; HIGH severity.

csharp:allowhtml.recordDesc: [AllowHtml] exempts one model property from request validation, so the property reaches views with its markup intact.
csharp:allowhtml.risk: An unencoded property that skips validation is a stored or reflected XSS path in every view that renders it; HIGH severity.

csharp:machineval.recordDesc: validationKey is set to a literal value in configuration, so the key that signs forms-authentication tickets is stored in the repository.
csharp:machineval.risk: Anyone who can read the repository can forge authentication tickets for that application; HIGH severity.

csharp:machinedec.recordDesc: decryptionKey is set to a literal value in configuration, so the key protecting encrypted configuration sections is stored in the repository.
csharp:machinedec.risk: A reader of the repository can decrypt protected sections such as connection strings; HIGH severity.

csharp:customerrors.recordDesc: customErrors mode="Off" makes ASP.NET return the detailed exception page to the client instead of a generic error.
csharp:customerrors.risk: Stack traces and configuration fragments disclose framework versions, paths and query shape to any unauthenticated request that provokes an error; HIGH severity.

csharp:trace.recordDesc: trace enabled="true" writes request diagnostics, including headers and submitted values, into the trace output.
csharp:trace.risk: Request diagnostics reach a page or file that may be readable, exposing session identifiers and submitted data; HIGH severity because the trace surface is reachable wherever the build runs.

csharp:debug.recordDesc: compilation debug="true" ships a build with debug symbols and the developer exception page enabled.
csharp:debug.risk: Debug output and source fragments are exposed wherever that build runs, and the build no longer behaves like the release build; HIGH severity.

title: Shell expansion of a variable ({fw}) — review required
description: A shell runs a variable's content: {sink} ({fw}). Variable content becomes command text. This lexical rule flags the expansion; the reviewer confirms trust or restructures via {safe}.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on shell expansion ({fw}).
fp: Trusted variables are the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {fw}, {sink} expands into command text. The remedy is {safe}.
verifyT: Rescan shows no expansion on untrusted input.

cweDef.name: Use of Externally-Controlled Input to Select Classes or Code ('Unsafe Reflection')
cweDef.summary: A class, method, or module name is chosen at runtime from input the program does not control, so the selected code runs. Reflection and dynamic lookup then reach code that was never meant to be selectable from outside.

title: Reflective invocation via {sink} ({lang}) — review required
description: The {lang} call {sink} selects a class, method, or module at runtime by name. If the name comes from untrusted input, the caller chooses which code runs. This lexical rule flags the call; the reviewer confirms the name is fixed or replaces it with {safe}.
remediation: Resolve names only from a fixed allow-list, or replace with {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: any {sink} call matches whether or not the name is user-controlled. Regex cannot prove data flow; a constant name is a false positive.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on the {sink} call in {lang} code.
fp: Constant names and framework-internal reflection are the common false positives.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} resolves code by name at runtime. The remedy is {safe}.
applicability: {lang} runtime name resolution; single-line lexical scope.
risk: Selection of unintended code or classes when the name is attacker-influenced; MEDIUM because the call alone does not prove data flow.
why: {sink} resolves a name at runtime in {lang}.
fix: Resolve names only from a fixed allow-list.
verifyT: Rescan shows no name resolution on untrusted input.

java:forname: a fixed allow-list of class names
java:getdeclared: a fixed allow-list of method names
ruby:public_send: an explicit allow-list of method names
csharp:gettype: a fixed allow-list of type names
apex: a fixed allowlist of class names
